speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing persistent vomiting and chest pain; please tell me, when did these symptoms first start and how would you describe the nature of the pain?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave Syndrome. Based on your history of forceful retching after heavy alcohol consumption followed by sudden chest pain and coughing, you likely have a ruptured esophagus. I will need to confirm this immediately with a Contrast Esophagogram or CT Chest.
